LLMs are really bad at reasoning. Chain of thought is expensive and internal reasoning circuits are limited. So why not build an architecture specifically for reasoning. That's what Tiny Recursive Models do. They recursively update latent reasoning and answer spaces. And because of this new training and inference procedure we can use smaller models. While Deepseek R1 has ~700 billion parameters it is incapable of playing Sudoko, 0% on sudoko-extreme. A TRM with 7 million parameters achieves 87.4% on the same benchmark. But applying the same weights to the same vectors is deterministic. If we add noise throughout the process we make a Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model, which achieved 98.75% on sudoku-extreme. I explore these tiny models in this notebook submitted to Marimo’s Notebook Challenge 2. I highly recommend the video explainer although I may be biased. Thanks to the marimo and alphaXiv teams for hosting this challenge and selecting such interesting papers! Paper: https://lnkd.in/gAWrKGxP Video Explainer: https://lnkd.in/gxvZ4jfg ...more

All my friends are too busy, so I'm building AI agents to play Minecraft with me instead. I'm at the Y Combinator office right now for HUD 's RSI and RL Environments hackathon - my ninth YC hackathon so far - and I decided to build something fun that'd also teach me more about these technologies. A few years ago, I saw a viral video about AI-powered Minecraft bots that "simulated civilization." They formed "cultures" and waged "wars." This piqued my curiosity immediately, and hasn't left my mind since. I thought it would be incredible to simulate factions of intelligent agents roaming an open world, gathering resources, dividing tasks, and achieving goals together. To my dismay, the project was closed-source, and no further updates have come out of it since that original demo. By 2026 standards, the technology available at the time that project was made is already aging. Multimodal LLMs, tool calling, structured output, reasoning, and the exponential improvement of the models overall make this project even more feasible than before - indeed, I think I can do better than the original if I continue beyond this hackathon! So far, the agents are capable of: - Navigating, fighting, gathering resources, and other basic abilities - Long and short-term planning and goals - Communicating with each other (or humans) to share info or divide tasks - Social intelligence - remembering good/bad interactions, holding grudges, etc. - "Imagining" and building complex structures Anyways, I'm posting this before the hackathon is even over for two reasons: 1. There's a Most Viral track 😅 2. I'd love to have humans play alongside my agents! If you'd like to play with the agents, comment or DM and I'll share access to a test server very shortly. ...more ...more

Big news from Boltz - our biggest update yet! 🚀 Today we’re releasing two new state-of-the-art models for protein design and small molecule hit discovery with extensive wet lab validation and a new API to run all of our models on scalable GPUs wherever you (or your agents) work today! 🔥 Read the TLDR below, or check out our blog post: https://lnkd.in/gZSwW7hm 🧬 BoltzMol-1 — Our first hit-discovery pipeline for small molecules that leverages an optimized version of Boltz-2 and our new suite of ADMET models for solubility, lipophilicity and permeability. We tested BoltzMol on a set of 10 difficult, previously unseen targets and got confirmed hits on 6, while only testing a small number of compounds for each (28–51) – a fraction of the cost of a traditional screening. 🔬 BoltzProt-1 — Our most powerful pipeline for protein design, powered by our new protein-protein affinity model (BoltzPPI) that prioritizes designs most likely to bind. We tested BoltzProt on a set of hard targets and found the model nearly tripled BoltzGen’s zero-shot nanobody hit rate, and in head-to-head comparisons with other leading proprietary models BoltzProt shows higher success. Beyond binding, we found that 58% of those binders pass a stringent multi-criteria developability panel, on par or better than clinical-stage therapeutic nanobodies. ⚡ The Boltz API — The fastest, cheapest and most flexible way to run Boltz models from just $0.025 per prediction on high-performance distributed compute. Built from the ground up for agentic workflows, the API is a powerful new set of primitives for drug discovery and molecular design. We’ve partnered with Anthropic , Benchling , Phylo , Amazon Bio Discovery, Rowan, Tamarind Bio , Kiin Bio , PAULING.AI , Mirror Physics and Cultivarium on first-party integrations so that our newest models and primitives are natively supported in your favorite tool. We’ve also built support for OpenAI Codex and Gemini CLI so you don’t have to choose. As always: you own your inputs and outputs, and we don't train on your data. To celebrate, we're giving $2,000 in API credits to every company and $100 to every academic for the first two weeks. Grab a key at api.boltz.bio and start designing today! Join us for our launch events: Boston (June 18th), San Francisco (June 22nd) and London (July 2nd). Sign-up links in comments. All credit goes to the entire Boltz team. It is humbling and energizing to work every day alongside such a talented, motivated, and focused small team. If you are excited by our mission, join us. You won’t regret it. ...more ...more

With so many exciting areas of AI advancement, one NeurIPS workshop was not enough. 😅 This year, I’m co-organizing/advising three (two in Sydney 🇦🇺 and one in my hometown of Atlanta 🇺🇸), each on unique topics! 👇 🍱 BeNTo | Sydney 🇦🇺 https://lnkd.in/eBi7gxCm With Sophia and Molei , and led by Minhyuk , Jaihoon , along with Subham and Nolan , for everyone thinking beyond autoregressive next-token prediction, this workshop will be all about new generative modalities: discrete diffusion and flows, parallel decoding, optimal transport, Schrödinger bridges, inference-time scaling, reward alignment, and more. 🤖 🧬 GEM | Atlanta 🇺🇸 https://www.gembio.ai/ For our AIxBio community, with Lauren , Chenghao , Jarrid, Soojung , Jacob , Sidney , and Nick , GEM is back for V4: DNA/RNA/peptide/protein design, biological sequence models, wet-lab validation, and new ML approaches for engineering biology. 🧑‍🔬🧑‍💻 We’ll also have opportunities for experimental validation (with Adaptyv ) and seed grants! 💸 ⚗️ SIMBIOCHEM II | Sydney 🇦🇺 https://simbiochem.com/ For the exciting field of simulation + molecular ML crowd, led by the fearless Bruno Trentini and team, our second iteration will focus on molecular dynamics, computational chemistry, biophysics, physics-informed generative models, enhanced sampling, and ML for understanding molecular systems, with GPUs up for grabs! 💽 All three have open calls for papers (due in about two weeks). If you have exciting new work that fits one of these communities, send us your best stuff on OpenReview and come hang out with us at NeurIPS in December! 🚀

I am speaking at a NICE webinar on September 16! The webinar is titled "Preparing Today's Students for Tomorrow's Cyber Careers," hosted by National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) . Faisal Abdullah and I will present "When Labs Have Stakes", which was the training approach we shared at the NICE Conference in June, and Rita Sabri will elaborate on her blueprint for teaching cloud security and GenAI to K-12 students. We will discuss how reality- and skills-based education can help students develop capabilities and hands-on experience that employers in 2026 are looking for. You can register for the webinar at this link: https://lnkd.in/ewh_q7sU

I am beyond privileged and thrilled to have experienced a summer full of learning, growth, and collaboration. I could not be more grateful for the trust she had in me for my first internship.
